reviews.comment: Prof. Hercot is genuinely a great professor. If you want to add spice to your life, I highly recommend FINC 449 and specifically with Prof. Hercot. The class is hard and he expects a lot from you, but you're going to get a lot out of it. Prof. Hercot is also there for his students and truly cares that you understand concepts and pursue excellence.

The option for FINC 710 was not listed. He is a good professor and cares about students. Expects a lot from students. Class is hard, but I learned. Finance is not my thing, but he wants students to succeed.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: One of the most difficult classes I have ever taken. However, it is also the class I have gotten the most out of during college. Hercot is such an intelligent and kind guy who can come off intimidating, but is a fabulous teacher. If you have the time to commit to this class, I highly recommend taking it. He will take care of your grade in the end.
very bad professor! he goes SO fast you cannot keep up! then will call on you to answer! he's very rude and i would not recommend him!

If you care about his class and the subject matter, you will enjoy the class. Professor Hercot cares deeply that his students are learning the material in this course, and he has high expectations of his students because he knows that they are capable. It's up to you to put in the work; if you want a good grade in this class, you'll have to earn it

Hercot is a great teacher and if you put in the work you will do well in this class. Attendance and participation is graded. There is only 2 exams, assignments almost every week, and a final group project. Overall, he helps you understand the topics very well from his lectures. If you are confused he is happy to help in office hours.

Don't expect your grade to be handed to you. If you put in the work and effort, you will be given the grade you deserve or even better. Participation is a big part of your grade, so make sure to ask questions or make comments. He is a nice prof and doesn't dwell on your mistakes (only intimidating for people in Aggies in Wallstreet).
Prof. Hercot demonstrates his passion for teaching in every lecture. He is demanding of students because he truly wants them to be the best at what they do. One of the best TEACHERS I've ever had.

Best professor I ever had. He has extensive real world experience and cares about helping his students succeed. This course is challenging and time consuming but super helpful for students who will be working in Investment Banking, Private Equity, etc. If you want to challenge yourself and actually learn valuable finance skills, take this course.

Professor Hercot gave lectures that were quick and sometimes would not answer questions in lecture. This class is based in some tests but largely on assignments and a group project. The assignments in this class are weekly and take about 5-10 hours to complete. Finally, professor Hercot largely taught what to do but not why you do it.

This is now my least favorite class and professor that I have taken at A&M, and I'm close to graduating so I've had plenty of experience at this point. Professor Hercot creates a hostile learning environment where he rips you apart for not knowing the right answer, and the class is extremely difficult and he doesn't do much to teach any of it.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Impossible class - the professor lacks empathy and in general is not a nice person. Clearly couldn't cut it in the real world and defaulted to academia. Avoid at all costs.

Professor Hercot is tough. The class is extremely difficult material, but he does not make it easier by having a thick French accent and by using terms that are different than most of the other Finance classes. Attendance is a must, but he will make you feel stupid constantly when he calls on you in class and you do not know the PERFECT answer.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Hercot provided one of the best learning experiences I have had A&M. It is hard. Really, really hard. But in the end, if you show up, pay attention and leave with more than you started with, he will take care of your grade at the end. Do not be late to class and participate and you will be fine. I would take Hercot again in a heartbeat.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: This class is hard. The class will constitute 85% of you classwork for the semester.  Worth it? Absolutely.  You will learn so much and acquire a VALUABLE lifelong skill. By far the best class I have taken in my entire undergrad in terms of knowledge and reward. Prof. is very blunt and can come off as mean. You better have a spine and work ethic.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Clearly the best class I have ever taken. The approach of the course is very practical. The professor wants to prepare you in the best way for the real world. I felt mentally challenged the whole semester and I acquired great knowledge. For this class, you will work a lot but learn a lot. Totally worth it for anyone who is interested into finance.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This is by far the best class I have ever had in my life. I learned so much during the semester both in excel and about finance in general, you have to work a lot in this class, but it is worth every single hour you spend. Phillipe Hercot is a great teacher that really cares about his students and making them perform their best.

Really mean french guy who is perpetually disappointed in you. Makes you feel stupid in front of peers if you don't know the exact answer to a question. Encourages participation but gets annoyed when you answer a question the wrong way. Avoid at all costs.
